slides.title: From Evidence Category to Strategy Component
bullets: This lesson looks at how RWE integrates into product medical strategy
RWE is now a core part of Integrated Evidence Generation Plans (IEGP)
IEGPs coordinate all research activity around a product

slides.title: What an IEGP Brings Together
bullets: Phase IIIb and IV studies, IIS collaborations, registry capabilities
Real-world data collection frameworks and HEOR studies
Goal: deliberate evidence, not scattered and reactive generation
Built to support access decisions, HCP questions, and long-term relevance

slides.title: Primary Source of Field Intelligence
bullets: Field insights feed directly into evidence-plan prioritization
Unanswered questions, uncertain subgroups, comparators of interest
Insights refine future protocol design and RWE and HEOR strategy
Keeps the plan aligned with real access and reimbursement needs

slides.title: The MSL as a Translator
bullets: MSL doesn't just communicate evidence outward to the field
Channels field evidence needs back into internal strategic planning
This translation function is a key differentiator of the MSL role
Recent Medical Affairs frameworks name it among the role's top values

slides.title: Structure, Not Anecdote
bullets: Needs structured processes for capturing and sharing insights
Needs trust with internal evidence, HEOR, and market access teams
So information flows in both directions systematically

takeaway.title: RWE now sits at the core of integrated evidence plans, and the MSL is the bidirectional link that keeps those plans grounded in the field
bullets: IEGPs coordinate Phase IIIb/IV, IIS, registries, RWE and HEOR together
Field insights directly shape evidence priorities and protocol design
Systematic insight capture, not anecdote, makes this translation work
